decision: The audit log records not just who approved a change but what happened afterwards
why: Trust in an agent should come from its track record: a sell-through lift, a rejected margin breach. Outcomes still in their window say so instead of guessing.
value: Reviewers can see whether the agent's proposals actually worked.

decision: Every AI entry opens 'How this was made': sources with scores, tool calls with latency, model route, eval score, tokens and simulated cost
why: Auditable AI means anyone can reconstruct a decision; the same record links to the harness trace.
value: Decisions are explainable to finance, legal and the next engineer.

decision: Approving a price writes a price.changed event; the audit log, the storefront and the data lake all subscribe
why: One event keeps every reader consistent and gives the audit trail a single source.
alternative: Each system writes its own audit rows.
value: What the customer sees and what the audit says can never disagree.

decision: Filters split agent proposals, human edits and rejections
why: The questions differ: 'what did the agent do?' vs 'where did people overrule it?'.
value: Answers to audit questions in one click.

decision: Each entry names the model route: fine-tuned small model by default, escalated to a large model with a reason
why: Routing is where cost and quality trade off; recording it per decision makes the trade-off reviewable.
value: Cheap by default, capable when needed, and visible either way.
